1. List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Satish Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Sanjay Tiwari, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Deepak Kumar Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.147 of 2024, under Sections 376, 328 I.P.C. and 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Belipar, District Gorakhpur, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text:
PROSECUTION STORY:
4. The applicant is stated to have established corporeal relationship with the daughter of the informant on the false promise of marriage and had subsequently refused to comply with the said promise.

5. On 11.05.2024 at about 6:00 p.m., the applicant is stated to have enticed her away and administered her some obnoxious material in a bottle of 500 m.l., thereby she started vomiting and her condition deteriorated and she was admitted to a private hospital by the police the same night at 9:30 p.m.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
6. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
7. The FIR is delayed and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
8. The medical report does not corroborate any allegations against the applicant.

Even the medical report, annexed as Annexure No.6 to the bail application, does not indicate that any investigation has been taken regarding ascertaining whether gastrointestinal lavage contained any poisonous material.
9. The victim was discharged from hospital on 13.05.2024 at 5:30 p.m. against the medical advice.
The same fact stands mentioned in the certificate dated 15.06.2024.
She has not been taken to any hospital after the said incident, as such the prosecution story stands falsified.
10. As per Class Vth transfer certificate of the victim, her date of birth is 01.07.2007, although by her appearance, she seems to be major.
11. The said certificate is not admissible in evidence.
12. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
13. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 20.06.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/INFORMANT:
14.
The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

CONCLUSION:

Yuvaprakash vs State Rep. by Inspector of Police, AIR 2023 SC 3525, the Supreme Court has observed that in the absence of records relating to the birth of the victim, no other documents except the Matriculation or equivalent certificate from the concerned examination board or certificate by a corporation, municipal authority or a Panchayat can be relied upon to ascertain the age of the victim.

sentences.text: 16. ?The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

17. ?A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
18.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ?Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
19.
?Learned A.G.A. could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
20. ?It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned A.G.A.
21.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

22. Let the applicant- Rajkamal Sahni involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to Rajkamal Sahni vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59467337/
3 treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

entities.text: Rajkamal Sahni vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 23. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

24. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

(Justice Krishan Pahal)
